thread:
maria: Follow-up on console-side policy checks: we need a clear low-latency pattern for dashboards. Blocking per-panel evals are risky.

alex: Agreed. Idea: two-step flow — pre-render batch 'policy-hint' and post-render patch for heavy rewrites. Pre-render must be bounded (10ms window).

ben: Benchmarks show single eval ~20ms. Batching across panels reduces median but increases tail if we wait too long. Suggest default batch_window_ms=8 and max_batch=96.

sasha: Console should accept three hint outcomes: allow, mask (client-side transform), or rewrite_template (deterministic). If rewrite_template present, try local transform else trigger a targeted re-fetch.

maria: Important: UI must not block full dashboard on hint; use async patching for non-critical panels. Add stale_allowed flag to panel config so product can choose.

jason: Token handling: console includes role-set + flags in the batch. QPL will not introspect tokens. This avoids duplicated caches.

alex: Telemetry: emit batch_size, eval_latency_p50/p95, rewrite_rate, stale_served_rate, fallback_count. Ops circuit: if p95>150ms for 3m flip to cached-decisions for that tenant.

ben: Privacy: record hashed request samples (<0.5%) for replay and rotate every 24h.

infra-bot: infra: queued qpl-canary deployment (v3) for 2 hosts in prod-canary. Logs: https://infra.internal/redwood/qpl/canary/3070001111

sasha: I'll include SDK patch to surface policy_hint_ttl and stale badge class.

maria: Action items: alex -> microbench + batching spike; ben -> SLO dashboard + replay hook; jason -> contract for role-set payload; sasha -> SDK + UI patch. I'll write the follow-up note and schedule a quick review.
